newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania slams Italy but security force goes ahead.
newsitem.headline: Albania slams Italy but security force goes ahead.

text.p: Albania lashed out at Italy on Saturday over the sinking of an illegal refugee boat as Rome prepared to send a multinational security force to its lawless neighbour to protect humanitarian relief operations.
Prime Minister Bashkim Fino went on television to demand an official investigation by Rome into the sinking of the refugee boat on Friday, in which at least four people drowned.

Thirty-four people were rescued and said dozens of others had been aboard when their boat collided with an Italian navy corvette, enforcing orders to turn back refugees fleeing from strife-torn Albania.

Italy disputes that many others were aboard the ill-fated boat which was crossing the southern Adriatic from the port of Vlore. More than 13,000 Albanians have fled to Italy in boats since an armed insurrection swept their country this month.
Albanian politicians and the public expressed outrage at the incident and said it stemmed from Italy's tough policy of blocking and turning back illegal refugee boats.
Fino called on Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi to start "investigations so the guilty can be identified. I still insist the tragedy should have been avoided."
The Albanian Foreign Ministry summoned Italian ambassador Paolo Foresti to demand that steps be taken to prevent such tragedies in future.
Other voices also criticised the handling of the boat incident and the handling of the Albanian crisis.

The semi-official Vatican newspaper L'Osservatore Romano said the deaths of the refugees were an "avoidable tragedy", and criticised the "bureaucratic slowness and indifference of part of the international community."

Prodi said the sinking of the boat had made Italy's planned international security mission to Albania more urgent but said the navy would continue to patrol the southern Adriatic and to stem the tide of refugees.
"This event shows that the international operation to help Albania has to begin as soon as possible," Prodi said.
The U.N. Security Council on Friday authorised the mission to send an Italian-led multinational security force to Albania to protect international relief operations.
Italy sees the relief operation as essential to stabilising the country to keep potential refugees at home and to pave the way for planned early national elections in June.
Other countries expected to join the multinational force are Greece, France, Spain, Portugal and perhaps Turkey and Romania.
The boat incident is unlikely to slow the deployment of the multinational force but it may sour the atmosphere in which the force operates in some parts of the country.
The force, expected to be around 2,500 troops or police, will be deployed to protect the Adriatic ports of Durres and Vlore, where many of those on the ill-fated boat came from.
It will also protect Tirana airport and convoys which will transport food and medical supplies throughout the country.
There has been no sign of famine or malnutrition but the Red Cross has warned that a collapse of the distribution system could threaten about 10 percent of the 3.4 million population.
In Durres, 670 tonnes of potatoes were unloaded on Saturday by a private company, which said there was no danger.

"The situation is calm and there is no problem. We can accept any kind of vessel and we are guaranteeing unloading and security," the port manager for the Adriatic Shipping Company, Petrit Hani, told Reuters Television.

Field workers for both the Medecins Sans Frontieres (Doctors Without Borders) and the Geneva-based International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) have expressed reservations about the need to embark on a large and heavily-guarded relief operation.
